text:
maria: Kicked off the HelioHealth POC perf sweep this morning. Baseline + quantized variants done for v1. Quick summary here.
lee: Nice, can you drop the raw numbers?
maria: Median latency (75 tokens): baseline 72ms, q4-8bit 59ms. 95p: baseline 140ms, q4 160ms. 99p: baseline 320ms, q4 spiked to ~980ms in a few runs.
devon: Whoa 99p spike — looks like KV/cache churn?
maria: Yep. We saw large variance when parallel requests hit different prompt prefixes. Cold-KV misses on quantized path are higher.
lee: Any reproducible command/snippet for the run?
maria: Run command we used:

```
./bench --model redwood-xl-v1 --variant q4_0 --seq 75 --qps 150 --concurrency 8 --prefetch true --ramp 600
```

maria: Also tried burst test: sustained 250 qps for 5m then 1k qps for 30s — quantized kept throughput but 99p tail blew up during spikes.
sam: Could that be memory paging on the quantized kernel?
devon: Likely. Need to validate kernel selection + cuda mem footprint. Alex from runtime can weight in.
alex: Looking. Initial hypothesis: quant kernels evict larger KV pages under bursty concurrent KV access. Working on a fix to pin hot KV pages and improve async prefetching.
maria: Customer (HelioHealth) asked two things: 1) can we meet 99p < 400ms at their target qps (600) in prod; 2) pricing for reserved burst capacity (3k qps peak); 3) confirm HSM/KMS + SOC2 is fine for PHI.
lee: For 1) with baseline model yes today in Dedicated; with current q4 we need pinning + better prefetching — could be a config change or small runtime patch. We should plan an A/B run.
devon: Ops run plan: do 3x 30m long steady-state runs across 3 AZs, include cold-start windows and synthetic prefix skew (50% unique prefixes). Collect traces and kernel metrics.
sam: I'll add memory/disk IO counters, nvlink usage, and kernel eviction logs.
ops-bot: Reminder: schedule load test slot on ded pool "ded-nyc-4g" — available 2026-06-12 02:00-05:00 UTC.
maria: Pricing question from procurement: what is monthly uplift for reserved 3k qps burst (guaranteed 10% headroom) vs pay-as-you-go? Need rough ballpark by EOD.
lee: Preliminary: reserved burst (1yr) + SLA + 99p targets ~ $22k/month add-on for that capacity profile. PAYG estimate for same bandwidth ~ $40k/month. (very rough)
alex: If runtime patch reduces 99p tail by 60% we can move them to q4 path and save ~18% on token cost estimates; detail in model-cost sheet.
maria: Security: HelioHealth asked for KMS key in their AWS account + HSM-backed signing. Legal asked if we have any blocking PCI/PHI items for a private deployment.
devon: Private deployment + customer-managed KMS is standard for Private. HSM: need to validate their FIPS/HSM vendor compatibility; we support AWS CloudHSM + external HSM via PKCS11 in our on-prem package.
sam: I'll attach the SOC2 + ISO docs link in the thread (posted after this), and ping compliance.
maria: Next actions:
- devon/lee/alex: run the 3x30m multi-AZ runs with kv-pin patch candidate and collect traces (target: run by 2026-06-12 window)
- sam: gather kernel/mem/IO counters and upload to shared folder
- maria: send pricing ballpark to Helio procurement by EOD and ask for expected go-live date
- ops-bot: allocate ded-nyc-4g slot and confirm

lee: one more — suggest putting a canary route that falls back to baseline model for tail requests (automatic fallback) while we iterate on q4 stability.
maria: Agreed. I'll propose that in the POC plan to Helio and add to the SOW.
alex: I'll open a runtime PR for kv pin + async prefetch and link here once ready.

maria: Thanks all. If we get tail to under 400ms 99p at 600 qps on Dedicated, sales ask is to push committed contract. :chart_with_upwards_trend:
sam: noted — will post logs and SOC docs shortly :white_check_mark:
ops-bot: Slot reserved: ded-nyc-4g, 2026-06-12 02:00-05:00 UTC.
